name: Confidential computing and privacy-preserving AI
summary: Hardware isolation and cryptographic methods allow sensitive data to be processed with reduced exposure to infrastructure operators or other parties.
useCase: Two organizations analyze sensitive records in an attested computing environment while limiting access to the underlying data.
whyNow: AI puts valuable private information into shared computing environments, raising the value of protecting data while it is in use. A consortium-commissioned IDC survey in 2025 found 18% of respondents in full production and 57% in pilots. Those categories should remain separate. Trusted execution environments, secure collaboration and fully homomorphic encryption solve related problems but have different costs and trust assumptions.

mainstream.scope: Attested confidential-computing environments used routinely for selected sensitive AI and regulated-cloud workloads.
mainstream.rationale: Production deployments and major-platform investment support a transition beyond pilots. Attestation, key management, software compatibility and independent assurance still add complexity. The date mainly concerns hardware-protected computing; it does not assume general-purpose fully homomorphic AI becomes economical on the same schedule.

direction: Growing, with limited comparable adoption data

metric.name: Survey respondents using confidential computing in full production
metric.scope: IDC survey commissioned by the Confidential Computing Consortium; 600 IT leaders across 15 industries in July 2025.
metric.limitations: One credible observed adoption point was identified; no historical growth rate can be calculated. It is a commissioned survey, not a market census. Combining pilots and production into a 75% production claim would be incorrect. The broad privacy-preserving-AI category has no consistent aggregate series.
metric.futureNote: The scenario expresses an analyst adoption judgment, not a measured growth curve. Future survey waves with a stable sample and definition are needed to quantify adoption growth.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: The consortium’s 2021 review described expanding projects, membership and attestation work.
A January update reported 36 corporate members, four nonprofit members and six projects after Q4 2021.
No comparable annual production-adoption measurement identified.
Apple described Private Cloud Compute and its hardware/software privacy architecture.
IDC surveyed 600 IT leaders; 18% reported full production, with 57% at pilot stage.
The consortium identified attestation, AI and practical deployment as priorities; no new comparable adoption percentage is inserted.

tailwinds: Sensitive AI workloads create demand for stronger data-in-use protection.
Cloud and processor support reduces the need to build every component from scratch.
bottlenecks: Attestation, keys, threat models and hardware trust must align across the full system.
Encrypted computation can impose substantial cost; an enclave alone does not prevent application-level data misuse.
watchMetrics: Stable-sample production adoption, separated from trials and planned deployments.
End-to-end overhead and independently verified protection for a clearly specified threat model.
